newsitem.title: USA: Miami, Fla., could see a $6.5 mln FY 1997 surplus.
newsitem.headline: Miami, Fla., could see a $6.5 mln FY 1997 surplus.

text.p: The city of Miami, Fla., said it projects a $6.5 million surplus for fiscal year 1997, based upon expenses and revenue data from the first quarter of the fiscal year, which ended December 31.
However, the city, in a report to its oversight board, said it still does not know how big of a carryover deficit it will have from fiscal 1996, which ended September 30.
The current fiscal 1997 budget is based on estimates that the carryover decifit for fiscal year 1996 was $19.4 million.
"I think the $19 million will change," said Jose Rodriguez, an auditor with KPMG Peat Marwick.
Asked whether the size of the 1996 deficit could rise or fall, Rodriguez said, "I don't know."

Rodriguez said he was still uncertain whether the auditing firm would have the fiscal 1996 audit completed as scheduled by March 31. The uncertainty came even after the oversight board agreed to send the city five more state auditors.

City Manager Ed Marquez presented the oversight board with the first actual revenue and expenditure numbers and budget projections. His repport made it clear that the city's auditing and accounting procedures need work.
At one pojnt during the presentation, overisght board chairman Lt. Gov. Buddy MacKay described the city's accounting procedure as "This is just like Alice in Wonderland."
